You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-divider-recolor
description: Solve ARC grids split by a solid horizontal divider, where the lower panel is extracted and its foreground recolored.

# Extract and recolor the lower panel

1. Compare each demonstration's full grid and output. Locate a uniform horizontal divider; check whether the output matches the panel below it, with the same width and height, rather than assuming the upper panel contributes.
2. Confirm the cell mapping against the demonstration: identify the lower-panel background and foreground, then verify which colors are preserved and which are recolored. Ignore the divider and upper panel only when the output evidence supports that crop.
3. Apply the demonstrated crop and color mapping to the test grid. Preserve the lower panel's dimensions and background, recolor only the demonstrated foreground, then verify every output row against the corresponding input row before submitting.

# Restore rectangle fields

1. Compare demonstrations cell by cell. Identify the background, repeated solid rectangular fields, and the specific noise color(s); infer each field's full bounds from its repeated fill, including cells replaced by noise. Confirm from outputs which noise is replaced by field fill inside a field and by background outside it. Do not assume every unusual color is noise or erase a field because some cells are corrupted.
2. Apply that rule to the test grid: fill anomalous cells within each established rectangle with its fill color; restore anomalous pixels outside all fields to the background. Preserve every uncorrupted field and background cell, even where its color also appears elsewhere as noise.
3. Check field bounds and all corrections row by row; ensure the output retains the input dimensions and that no unrelated cell changed before submitting.

Fields can differ in size and color. Do not infer a color's role from its numeric value alone; use demonstrated spatial roles and output changes.
